newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai central bank says baht at 32/dlr too low.
newsitem.headline: Thai central bank says baht at 32/dlr too low.

text.p: The Thai baht's fall to 32 per dollar is too low a level for the currency, the deputy governor of the Bank of Thailand said on Friday.
Chaiyawat Wibulswasdi told reporters that the central bank also did not expect the embattled currency to fall much further.

"The Bank of Thailand believes the baht has already declined substantially. Although there is possibility of its further fall depending on various factors, exporters should not expect the baht to fall further," Chaiyawat said.

The deputy governor said a comprehensive economic package expected to be announced by Finance Minister Thanong Bidaya in early August would include measures proposed by the central bank. He did not elaborate.

Chaiyawat attributed the baht's steady decline this week to expectations by Thai exporters that the currency would face further setbacks. He said such forecasts prompted exporters to delay selling their dollar positions in the hope of further gains against the baht.

The deputy bank governor said Thai foreign reserves have also declined due to reduced capital inflows, recent central bank intervention to defend the baht, and decisions by some foreign creditors not to renew short-term Thai debts.
He said the Bank of Thailand would move to ensure that the country has sufficient foreign reserves. "We would not rule out any options of boosting our reserves," he said without elaborating.
Thai foreign reserves fell to $33.3 billion at end-May from $37.3 billion a month earlier. Analysts expected the June reserves figure, due to be released on July 31, to fall further.

Finance Minister Thanong on Friday also did not deny the possibility of Thailand seeking financial assistance from the International Monetary Fund (IMF) and the Bank of Japan to help overcome short-term liquidity problems.
